checks.label: Vector components describe the separate x, y and z values of a vector: the readout's column lists arrow a's x and y values and the box arrow's x, y and z values, the same numbers as their i, j and k parts, and drawn nose to tail those parts end at the tip
Dragging the tip sets the parts: for every square the tip can reach, the column and the i and j readout give its across and up moves, and the dashed parts still end at the tip

At every whole angle from 0° to 90° the 10 N pull resolves into 10 cos θ across and 10 sin θ up: the readout shows both to two decimal places, the cos label sits on the across side next to the angle, each part is shorter than 10 N unless the pull lies along an axis, and Pythagoras on the parts gives back 10 N

Switching the 10 N pull to a bearing moves only the angle and its labels: the arrow, its parts and its column stay the same, the angle reads 30° off the x-axis and then a bearing of 060, the same 60° shows at the tip where the north part meets the arrow, and the cos label moves from the across side to the north side

With a bearing the angle sits next to north, so north takes the cosine: the ship's and the winch rope's pictures mark the bearing again at the tip, on the north part, and their right answers put cos on that side, giving 12 sin 30° = 6 knots east, and 43.3 N east with −25 N north; the winch's wrong picks point on bearings 150 and 060

Every number in the puzzles follows from the rule: 20 cos 60° = 10 and 20 sin 60° = 17.32; 12 cos 30° = 10.39; √(25 + 144) = 13 against 5 + 12 = 17 and 5 − 12 = −7; √13 = 3.61 and √49 = 7; √32 = 5.66, 4 + 4 + 7 = 15 and √81 = 9
A calculator's tan⁻¹(4 ÷ −3) gives −53.13°, pointing right and down, the opposite way to −3i + 4j; turned through 180° it lands on the arrow at 126.87°, and Pythagoras gives its size, 5

Turning the box changes only the view: at every turn from −55° to −10° its parts still run 2 across, 3 along and 6 up, nose to tail to the tip, the floor line reads 3.61 and the size 7, while the tip moves on the page
Every puzzle offers three different answers with exactly one accepted, gives each wrong one its own hint, and draws a wrong pick in red but a right one without
Before Check no puzzle's picture shows its answer, and a right answer shows it
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s
